question: does any public dataset satisfy all three CBRA properties (venue for H3)?

candidates.note: the only corpus with all three; but the boundary residual is not estimable on it (B1 = 29% vs 60% bar) -- viable but the signal is not there / is confounded by sedation-TTM-pressors. Viability is not the blocker here; estimability is.
ECG + drug timing + length, but BIS INDEX not raw EEG (fails p1), and essentially pure I+ (almost all surgical patients recover; fails p2). Confirmed by the Sci Data descriptor.
ECG + long ICU records + outcome contrast, but no concurrent raw EEG (fails p1).
raw EEG (+ ECG in SHHS/MASS) and length, but sleep is a reversible I+ transition with no I- non-recovery contrast (fails p2).
raw EEG and length, but typically no concurrent cardiac channel and no I-status contrast (fails p1 and p2).

preregistered_criterion: all three properties in one public corpus => new venue; else not executable, bottleneck is data
binding_constraint: raw EEG + concurrent cardiac + I+/I- contrast co-occurring (VitalDB has the clean transition but only BIS + pure-I+)
verdict: POSITIVE ARM NOT EXECUTABLE ON PUBLIC DATA (as of 2026-09) -- the bottleneck is data, and the binding constraint is the I+/I- contrast coexisting with raw EEG. Of the credible public candidates (5/5 hosts reachable, so access is not the issue), I-CARE is the ONLY corpus clearing all three properties -- and it fails not on viability but on estimability (B1 = 29%). Every other candidate fails a specific property: VitalDB gives a BIS index not raw EEG and is essentially pure I+; MIMIC has no concurrent EEG; sleep banks have no I- non-recovery contrast; seizure banks lack concurrent cardiac and an I-status contrast. So H3's re-test on a cleaner cohort has NO public venue: a healthier cohort with a clean consciousness transition (surgical emergence) exists in VitalDB but only as BIS and pure-I+, which cannot carry the I+/I- dissociation. The positive arm is data-limited, and confirming that is Paper 2's honest §14.2 estimability-condition result strengthened, not weakened.
